pr_snapshot.body:
VP8’s fixed16x16 pointer SAD caller rebuilt slice spans and widened row reductions on ARM. Use the caller-proved window, exact uint16 accumulation and a full-SAD path when limit>=65280. Keep the public wrapper inline; architecture-specific dispatch preserves the existing x64/scalar paths.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go1.27.2, PGO off, six balanced rounds:
- Early exits:1.78–1.81x faster than merged main and1.11–1.12x faster than assembly; every pair exceeds1.5x versus main.
- Limits>=65280:1.43–1.48x faster than main and2.79–2.82x faster than assembly. All20 cases beat both baselines in all six pairs, with zero allocations.
- Whole VP8 medians:0.99% slower at300 frames (2/6 faster),0.82% slower at60 frames (3/6 faster). No overall speedup claimed; ARM still trails assembly by7.9–10.9% on these workloads. Retain the verified kernel wins independently.

Full native tests, pixel/DSP purego+nosimd, SAD race/checkptr2, invalid-window subprocess checks and AMDv1 Rosetta correctness pass. Generated AMD callers/scalar body match main exactly; ARM callers directly invoke the new kernel. All23 public non-timing fields match. The native x64 harness now includes114 component cases. Refreshed PGO profile/fingerprint and source/build-selection gates pass.

Raw measurements, scalar correctness evidence, source hashes and rejected prototypes are under benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-arm64/2026-10-17-sad-limit. Preserve merged PR27 native x64/optimized-libvpx data separately under benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-amd64/2026-10-17-picker-filter. README unchanged.
